subject: Dedicated pilot: token economics & GPU lane proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Dedicated pilot: token economics & GPU lane proposal

Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can get a pilot scoped and priced: 

Summary of what you shared (please correct anything):
- Production use: clinical note summarization and triage prompts (mix of short and long contexts).
- Peak traffic: ~45 requests/sec during business hours; typical requests average ~2k tokens (prompt+response).
- Target monthly volume: you estimated 80–140M tokens/month depending on adoption.
- Budget range: you indicated ~$6k–$12k/mo for the pilot production runway (flexible).

What we need to confirm to produce a dedicated-lane quote:
1) Preferred GPU family: you mentioned being open to H100 but asked for H100 vs A100 latency tradeoffs.
2) Commitment tier: pilot = 1 reserved lane (dedicated GPU) with ability to burst to 2 lanes for short windows — confirm if that matches your expectations.
3) Target unit econ: is the target ~$6–$10 per 1M tokens (you said $/1M between $5–$12 on the call) or should we size around $7.5/1M as a mid point?

Proposed next steps from our side:
- Marissa will produce a short quote showing: 1x H100 reserved lane (baseline), burst path to 2 lanes, expected token throughput, and a target $/1M tiered price at 80M and 140M committed tokens.
- We'll attach a token-modeling sheet (baseline estimates + conservative headroom) and a preliminary quote PDF.
- If that looks good, we can issue a pilot PO + 30 day test period and set a follow-up call to finalize procurement.

Would love confirmation on the three items above (GPU family preference, burst behavior, and a firm target $/1M if you have one) so Marissa can finalize the quote.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

Attachments: edgehealth_token_modeling.xlsx (token scenarios), — spreadsheet with low/med/high adoption projections
From: Sarah Cole <sarah@edgehealth.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@edgehealth.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2027 17:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot: token economics & GPU lane proposal

Thanks Karthik — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed items:
- GPU: leaning toward H100 for the pilot due to lower latency on longer contexts, but cost sensitivity matters. Happy to see comparative numbers.
- Burst: yes — baseline 1 reserved lane, ability to burst to 2 lanes for ~2–3 hours/day at peak.
- Token estimate: our product team modeled (conservative) 95M tokens/month for the first 3 months, with upside to ~130M if adoption increases.

Budget guidance: procurement gave a soft target of $7–9 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot. That can be traded against other levers (commitment term, minimum monthly commit).

Procurement note: please include SOC2 Type II evidence and a simple SOW that we can attach to a PO. 

I'll review your modeling attachment and loop Tom from infra if we need deeper throughput details.

— Sarah Cole
Head of Product | EdgeHealth
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah@edgehealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2027 09:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated pilot: token economics & GPU lane proposal

Hi Sarah — looping in pricing and infra notes. Attached is a short preliminary quote (redwood_prelim_quote_20271010.pdf) and a brief throughput note. Highlights: 

Config options we priced: 
- Option A (latency-optimized): 1x H100 reserved lane (baseline), burst policy to 2x H100 for up to 3 hrs/day. Estimated baseline sustained throughput: ~30–35k tokens/sec (aggregate), supports your 45 req/s @ 2k tokens with modest queuing assumptions for short bursts.
- Option B (cost-optimized): 1x A100 reserved lane, burst to 2x A100. Lower baseline throughput per lane vs H100; better $/GPU-hour but higher $/1M tokens at peak.

Unit economics (preliminary, inclusive of our reserved-lane discount at pilot commit):
- At 95M tokens/mo commit: $7.5 per 1M tokens (Option A, H100 baseline).
- At 130M tokens/mo commit: $6.8 per 1M tokens (Option A, negotiated tier).
- Option B (A100) adds ~12% to the $/1M token estimate for comparable throughput.

Assumptions called out in the sheet: tokenization ratio, average response length, KV cache hit % for repeated prompts. If you have historical tokenization samples we can plug them in to tighten the estimate.

Next steps we propose: 
1) You confirm pilot commitment (target month-to-month token baseline or minimum commit).
2) We issue a formal quote + SOW and provide SOC2 evidence link for procurement.
3) Pilot run: 30–60 day window with telemetry access to validate actual $/1M and latency SLOs; final committed tier set after pilot.

Ben — can you include a short latency-vs-cost note for H100 vs A100 to share with Sarah's infra team?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: redwood_prelim_quote_20271010.pdf

- Procurement will expect SOC2 link + SOW in the quote; procurement@edgehealth.ai will track PO.

Please send the formal quote and SOW and we'll route an internal PO. Once PO is in flight, can we have a short kickoff with infra (Tom) to validate throughput profiles? 

Thanks — Sarah
